text:
Priya: Quick question — should route-specific view bindings be their own resource or nested under views? PM wants a cheap preview/apply flow that shows token cost and a diff before applying. Thoughts?

Samir: lean to top-level 'bindings' resource. Bindings have lifecycle (drafts, canaries, audit) so separate endpoints make sense. We can add /bindings?scope=route:r_99 and include staged_overrides.

Jia: top-level is fine, but keep the UI path simple: saved views list -> "Bind to route" -> modal that shows preview and cost. Backend can store binding id.

Dana: UX: preview must show a diff against current route filters and an estimated tokens/day. Include quick rollback link. Also let users choose canary ramp (e.g., 5%, 20%, 100%).

Lena: telemetry: emit events for preview and apply. preview event should include tokens_estimate and sample_rate; apply should include rollout_id and ramp_percent. Dont forget last_applied_by/at on binding metadata.

Samir: Implementation note: staged_overrides stored on the binding object so edits don't touch canonical view. Add version field on saved_view and binding points to version. Example payload in PR will show shape.

Priya: Nice. What about cost API? Do we call billing estimator sync during apply modal?

Jia: yes, call estimator on modal open with route_id + view_id + expected_qps. Show tokens/day and cost delta. If route is high traffic warn and auto-suggest throttles.

deploy-bot: canary deploy for ui-bindings-preview v1.2.0 started in prod-us-1 :rocket:

Dana: I'll mock modal with diff + cost chip and a small 'Apply as canary' dropdown. Will share Figma in this thread.

Priya: Action items: Samir PR for bindings model + migration, Lena telemetry spec, Dana Figma + copy, Jia do estimator infra handshake. Target: short canary next week.
